runs.title: Trace SSH wheel ownership
runs.prompt: In railmux ssh, explain how a mouse-wheel event over an agent pane is served from the fast client's local history overlay rather than forwarded upstream. Point to the exact implementation symbols and one existing focused test that directly asserts empty forwarded_input. Then suggest one small additional assertion.
runs.response:
railmux ssh — agent-pane wheel served locally, not forwarded upstream:

1. handle_terminal_part gets the SgrMouseEvent and dispatches to LocalHistoryView.wheel.
2. wheel() resolves the pane via _route_at; a hit on an agent viewport scrolls _HistoryViewport.offset and returns HistoryAction with render_history=True and forwarded_input=b"" — no upstream input.
3. apply_history_action only sends upstream when action.forwarded_input is set; empty means nothing reaches tmux. The overlay is painted client-side via surface.paint_overlays.
4. This is a fast-client history overlay over bounded snapshots, not tmux copy-mode; the implementation notes stock tmux WheelUpPane would enter copy-mode, which is deliberately avoided.

Focused test: tests/test_fast_full_window.py::test_local_history_routes_sidebar_immediately_and_owns_agent_wheel asserts agent_action.forwarded_input == b"".

Suggested addition: assert agent_action.render_history is True, proving the overlay rendered rather than merely dropping the event.

runs.title: Verify responsive layout gates
runs.prompt: Explain why a 76x30 Railmux terminal uses the compact single-page projection while a 160x38 terminal remains in the ordinary wide sidebar-plus-agent layout. Cite the exact responsive-layout symbols and one existing focused test. Suggest one website-recorder assertion that prevents a desktop demo from accidentally using compact mode.
runs.response:
presentation_for_geometry() selects the projection from geometry with hysteresis.

From WorkspacePresentation.WIDE it enters COMPACT when either dimension is cramped: width < COMPACT_ENTER_WIDTH (80) or height < COMPACT_ENTER_HEIGHT (24).

76x30: width 76 < 80, so it returns COMPACT even though 30 rows clear the height gate.
160x38: 160 ≥ 80 and 38 ≥ 24, so it stays WIDE with sidebar plus agent. COMPACT_EXIT_WIDTH/HEIGHT (84/26) only applies once already compact.

Existing focused test: tests/test_agent_workspace.py::test_compact_presentation_uses_two_dimensional_hysteresis pins both width and height behavior.

Recorder guard: pass each non-mobile profile through presentation_for_geometry and assert WorkspacePresentation.WIDE.

runs.title: Explain workspace layout
runs.prompt: Read src/railmux/ui/workspace.py only. In 3 concise sentences, explain what Railmux's F8 layout cycle does, how compact presentation differs from the saved layout, and why switching or hiding panes does not stop their agents. Name the exact relevant symbols. Do not modify files.
runs.response:
F8 uses `next_workspace_layout()` to cycle `WorkspaceLayout.SINGLE → SIDE_BY_SIDE → STACKED → SINGLE`.
`WorkspacePresentation.COMPACT` preserves `AgentWorkspace.layout` but shows one full-window `WorkspacePage` at a time via `AgentWorkspace.compact_page`.
Page switching only changes presentation, while `collapse_to_primary()` hides the secondary outer pane and preserves its detached agent identity in `AgentWorkspace.collapsed_secondary_agent`, so the agent keeps running.
